reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: Most of the simulated 84 % comes from the oil-free, thicker parent layer compared with an oil-containing baseline; the skin itself contributes a factor ~0.7 at ideal alignment, less when sprayed; about 60 % lower leaching overall is plausible. The platelet skin stiffens the surface in-plane and raises barnacle release stress, so the net contribution to time-averaged friction is about 0.5 %.
key_assumption_issues: Baseline is an oil-containing coating; against oil-free silicones the benefit is much smaller
Ideal Nielsen tortuosity with perfectly aligned platelets
Release penalty of the stiffened skin not simulated
killer_risks: Barrier skin raises in-plane stiffness and spreads fouler loads, degrading the foul-release function it is meant to protect
Crack initiation at platelet edges under cyclic strain
Poor platelet alignment in sprayed films

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The 50 % equals the assumed settlement factor; field results of microtextures against barnacles are much weaker and species-dependent than lab results, so about 25 % fewer settled barnacles is realistic. Valleys of ~40 um can host diatom slime, offsetting part of the gain; about 0.5 % of time-averaged friction.
key_assumption_issues: Settlement reduction factor 0.5 is an input from lab studies
Cyprid transport through a 1 mm layer with an assumed effective diffusivity
Diatom colonisation of the texture not modelled
killer_risks: Diatom slime prefers the wrinkle valleys and raises the slime penalty
Wrinkles flatten by creep of the soft base or wear off the crests within years
Large-area controlled wrinkling on a hull is not an established process

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The contact-shear reduction is set by assumed friction coefficients and an unproven 80 % intact fraction; Mg/Na competition weakens seawater alginate gels, so about 30 % lower average traction is realistic. Calcium-bridged anionic surfaces promote diatom and bacterial EPS adhesion, so the time-averaged drag is likely slightly worse than the baseline.
key_assumption_issues: Intact fraction 0.8 from assumed self-healing, not demonstrated
Friction coefficient of a seawater alginate gel (0.05) assumed
No model of fouling on an anionic, Ca-bridged surface
killer_risks: Promotes slime adhesion via Ca2+ bridging of EPS
Weak Mg-alginate gels in seawater provide little lubrication
Abraded anchored chains are not replaced
